articles.title: The Card Marked ‘Lead Organizer’
articles.summary: On Saturday morning, Lin Qiao only wants to open her pottery stall on time, but a ‘lead organizer’ card she never applied for sends her to distribute keys. After she hands it back, the emails and forms keep finding her.
articles.summaryZh: 周六早上，林桥只想按时摆好自己的陶杯，却被一张从未申请过的“主理人”卡叫去分钥匙。她把卡交回后，邮件和表格仍在继续找她。
storyParagraphs: At 8:30 on Saturday morning, the community craft market was suddenly short one person to guide new vendors through setup, and six carts were already jammed at the entrance. Lin Qiao had just carried her box of pottery mugs to her stall when a volunteer stopped her. “You’ve got the lead-organizer card, right? Can you hand out the keys first?” Lin Qiao looked down at the freshly printed card on her chest. She had never applied for that role.

The volunteer opened the sign-in folder. Beside Lin Qiao’s name were several entries in a row: “closing,” “key handover,” “new-vendor placement.” The first had happened simply because she lived nearby; later someone had casually passed her the keys, and after that the Saturday morning rota began listing her by default. The storage system also allowed only someone marked “lead organizer” to sign out spare tables. New vendors who saw the badge began bringing extension-cord requests, stall-number questions, and late-arrival notices straight to her.

Lin Qiao wanted to take the badge off, but two last-minute vendors were waiting for spare tables, so she signed them out first. Half an hour later, the coffee vendor handed her the backup card terminal for safekeeping because her name was also listed as the emergency contact on the insurance sheet. By the time Lin Qiao finally returned to her own stall, her first regular customers had already passed by. A whole box of pottery mugs was still unopened, and she started selling twenty-five minutes late.

In the afternoon, she put the keys, the card terminal, and the badge together on the coordination table. Before she could leave, the storage manager brought over the following week’s key confirmation, with her name still filled in automatically. Then a newcomer held up a phone showing the welcome email: “When you arrive, find Lin Qiao to confirm your stall.” Lin Qiao first walked the newcomer to the correct place, then worked with the coordinator to change the following week’s key list to a three-person rotation and asked for the insurance contact to follow the same rota.

The list changed, but the old pathways did not disappear at the same time. The next day, a supplier still sent Lin Qiao a ‘lead organizer confirmation’ using the old directory. On Monday, someone emailed her the stall map for the next market, and the storage reminder was still generated from the previous cycle’s data. While she forwarded the messages one by one, a vendor dragged over two electric kettles and asked whether, since she was still the contact, both could use the thin extension cable. Lin Qiao felt the cable’s casing warming and sent him to a wall socket instead. She removed her name from the contact fields she could edit, but another new message appeared in the forwarding queue.

At 8:25 the next Saturday, three rota cards lay on the entrance table. Lin Qiao’s said only “Vendor.” The card beside it said “Lead Organizer This Week.” She set down her pottery box and peeled back the first layer of foam. Someone was already pushing a cart through the entrance.
storyParagraphsZh: 周六上午八点半，社区手作市集临时少了一个带新人布展的人，入口已经堵着六辆推车。林桥刚把自己的陶杯箱搬到摊位，就被志愿者叫住：“主理人卡在你这儿吧？先帮大家分钥匙。”她低头看见胸前那张刚打印的卡，自己明明从没申请过这个身份。
志愿者翻开签到夹，林桥名字后面连续写着“收尾”“钥匙交接”“新人带位”。第一次只是因为她住得近，后来有人顺手把钥匙交给她，再后来周六早班直接排到她名下。仓库系统也只允许“主理人”签备用桌。新摊主看到胸卡，便把延长线、摊位号和迟到通知都先拿来问她。
林桥本想摘卡，可两个临时增加的摊主正等着备用桌，她只好先签。半小时后，咖啡摊主又把备用刷卡机塞给她保管，因为保险联系人表上的紧急姓名也是她。等林桥终于回到自己的摊位，第一批熟客已经走过，桌上还有一整箱陶杯没拆，开摊晚了二十五分钟。
午后，她把钥匙、刷卡机和胸卡一起放回协调桌。可还没离开，仓库管理员拿来下一周钥匙确认，系统仍自动带出她的名字；一名新人也举着手机过来，欢迎邮件写着“到场后找林桥确认摊位”。林桥先把新人送到位置，再和协调员把下周钥匙名单改成三人轮值，同时请对方把保险联系人改到轮值表对应的人。
名单改了，旧路径却没有同时消失。第二天供应商仍按旧通讯录给她发“主理人确认”，周一又有人把下一场摊位图直接发到她邮箱；仓库提醒也仍沿用上一周期的数据。林桥正逐封转发，一名摊主拖来两只电热水壶，问既然她还是联系人，能不能把它们都插在那根细延长线上。林桥摸到线皮已经发热，叫他换到墙边插座。她删掉自己能改的联系人栏，转发框里却又跳出一封新邮件。
下个周六八点二十五，入口桌上放着三张轮值卡。林桥那张只写“摊主”，旁边另一张写“本周主理人”。她把自己的陶杯箱放上桌，先拆了第一层泡沫纸。入口已经有人推车进来。
explanationParagraphs: Social construction describes how an identity, meaning, or social fact can become stable through repeated classification, institutional records, language, and mutual expectations, then go on to distribute real opportunities, responsibilities, risks, and resources.

This does not mean reality is fictional. Material constraints remain; the question is how a particular social meaning becomes institutionalized and why changing a label once does not immediately erase its effects.
explanationParagraphsZh: 社会建构指某种身份、意义或社会事实通过重复分类、制度记录、语言与相互期待逐渐稳定，并反过来真实分配机会、责任、风险和资源。
这不等于现实是虚构的。物质边界仍存在；关键是特定社会意义怎样被制度化，以及为何不能靠一次改名立刻消失。
articles.overall: “Lead organizer” is not a single database error. Lin Qiao’s early acts of helping entered sign-in records and key handovers, then were carried forward through the rota, sign-out permissions, insurance contact, newcomer emails, and supplier directory. Those records shaped what others expected from her, and those expectations created still more situations in which work was routed to her. The rotation changes later, but old records retain momentum. Pottery can still break and electrical loads can still exceed a cable’s capacity regardless of the label.
articles.overallZh: “主理人”不是一次数据库误标。林桥最初的顺手帮忙进入签到与钥匙交接，随后又被排班、签出权限、保险联系人、新人邮件和供应商通讯录相互承接；这些记录进一步塑造别人对她的期待，期待又让更多事务继续落到她手里。改成轮值后旧数据仍有惯性，但陶杯破碎、电路负载等物质约束不受标签支配。

module.intro: Once repeated classification enters permissions, rotas, and communication records, it guides other people’s actions and feeds new responsibilities back into the system. Changing the identity requires practices, records, and shared expectations to move together.
module.diagramTitle: How repeated classification becomes a social identity with real effects
diagramSteps: A convenient classification first enters everyday records
Several institutional processes begin carrying the same classification forward
Other people form stable expectations around that classification
Those expectations generate new records and responsibilities
After reclassification, old records and expectations still have to be changed over time
diagramStepNotes: Lin Qiao is first recorded because she lives nearby and often helps with closing; there is no natural “lead organizer” quality that makes the role inevitable.
The sign-in sheet, key permissions, rota, insurance contact, emails, and supplier directory reinforce one another, ruling out a single-point labeling error.
New vendors, the storage manager, and suppliers all act on the same classification, making it part of their practical expectations.
The more people route work to Lin Qiao through that identity, the more places in the system continue to record her that way, creating feedback between practice and expectation.
Even after the rota changes, old reminders and directories continue to point to her, showing that social facts have inertia while material conditions remain independent of the label.
mapping: Early closing and key handovers → the starting material for the classification.
Sign-in records, permissions, rota, insurance, and emails → institutional records that reinforce one another.
A twenty-five-minute late opening → a real time cost produced by the social identity.
The old supplier directory still pointing to Lin Qiao → persistence of expectations after reclassification.
Three rota cards → a social identity can be reorganized, but practices and records must change with it.
module.boundary: Social construction does not mean that all reality is created arbitrarily by words, or that changing a label makes its consequences disappear. Whether pottery breaks or a circuit overloads does not depend on an identity label. This example concerns only how the social identity of “who counts as the lead organizer” acquires stable effects through repeated practice, institutional records, and mutual expectations. The people, market, and systems are fictional.
module.reflection: Why is removing “lead organizer” from one badge not enough, if the key permissions, rota, contact lists, and other people’s expectations still point in the old direction?

moduleZh.intro: 重复分类一旦进入权限、排班和沟通记录，就会成为别人行动的依据，并把新的责任和后果继续写回制度。改变身份需要同时改动实践、记录与共同期待。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 重复分类怎样变成具有现实后果的社会身份
diagramSteps: 便利性的分类先进入日常记录
多个制度环节开始承接同一分类
他人据此形成稳定的行动期待
期待反过来增加新的记录与责任
重新分类后旧记录和期待仍需逐步改写
diagramStepNotes: 林桥最初只是因为住得近、常收尾而留下交接记录，不存在天然的“主理人”属性。
签到、钥匙权限、排班、保险联系人、邮件和供应商通讯录相互承接，排除了单点误标的解释。
新摊主、仓库管理员和供应商都据此找她，分类开始成为别人行动的依据。
越多人按这个身份把事务交给她，系统里越多地方继续记录她，形成实践与期待的反馈。
改轮值后旧提醒和旧通讯录仍继续指向她，说明社会事实有惯性，而物质条件并未被标签创造。
mapping: 最初的收尾与钥匙交接 → 分类形成的起点。
签到、权限、排班、保险和邮件 → 相互承接的制度记录。
晚开摊二十五分钟 → 社会身份带来的真实时间代价。
旧通讯录继续找林桥 → 改名后仍存在的期待惯性。
三张轮值卡 → 社会身份可以重组，但需要同步改变实践与记录。
moduleZh.boundary: 社会建构不是说所有现实都由说法任意创造，也不是说改一个称呼就能让后果消失。陶杯会不会碎、电路是否过载等物质条件不由身份标签决定；本例只讨论“谁被当作主理人”这一社会身份如何通过重复实践、制度记录和相互期待获得稳定后果。人物、市集和制度均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么把“主理人”从一张胸卡上删掉还不够，而要连钥匙权限、排班、联系人和他人的期待一起改变？

references.use: Used to support the idea that everyday knowledge, institutionalization, objectivation, and socialization jointly form and maintain social reality, and that socially produced orders can confront individuals as objective facts.

references.use: Used to support the need to specify what is constructing what in social-construction claims, to distinguish representations, human categories, and more general facts, and to avoid treating local construction as if all material reality could be changed arbitrarily.

referencesZh.use: 用于支持日常知识、制度化、客观化与社会化共同形成并维持社会现实，以及社会产生的秩序会以客观事实的形式反过来约束个人。

articles.title: The Blue Tags That Stayed Separate
articles.titleZh: 蓝标签没有被并到一起
articles.summary: After twelve years in the wholesale flower market, Xu Lan combines three buckets of white tulips on her first day in a wedding studio. She understands the blue tags, but when the phone and trolley arrive together, her hands still send the flowers toward their old place.
articles.summaryZh: 做了十二年批发花市的许岚，第一天便把三桶同色郁金香并到一起。她已经读懂蓝签，可电话和推车同时出现时，手仍先把花送往旧位置。
storyParagraphs: At 7:00 on Monday morning, Xu Lan began her first day at a wedding-flower studio, with four table arrangements due by 9:00. She had spent twelve years in the wholesale flower market and could tell at a glance which bucket needed topping up and which bunch should move first. But as soon as she combined three buckets of white tulips, the lead florist pulled two of them apart again. The flowers were the same color, but the blue tags showed different clients and table numbers, and the stems had deliberately been left at different lengths.

Xu Lan reread all three blue tags and repeated aloud, “Same color still doesn’t mean same order.” Ten minutes later, the phone rang just as a delivery trolley blocked the aisle and two bunches of fast-opening peonies stood in the way. While talking, she had already moved the bunches closest to the door. In the wholesale market, that move did two useful things at once: it cleared the trolley and brought flowers that needed to move quickly closer to dispatch. When a colleague later came looking for the bride’s afternoon bouquet, one bunch had been mixed into another order. It took fifteen minutes to rebuild the correct combination of stems.

When the second delivery trolley arrived that morning, Xu Lan again cleared the aisle first, and this time the move worked perfectly. The driver passed without delay and even told her she was good at making space. But Xu Lan also slid a nearby bucket of fast-opening white flowers forward. When she turned back to the table order, she saw that the blue tag had rotated inward and the bucket had nearly been absorbed into the nearest order again. She turned the tag outward and, for the first time, treated “make way for the trolley” and “decide which order the flowers belong to” as two separate actions.

On the second day, she gave herself one small practice: touch the blue tag before taking any flowers. Twice that morning, her hand had already moved toward a same-color bucket before touching the plastic tag and changing direction. By the afternoon, when the trolley came through, she moved only empty buckets and cleared the aisle without shifting order flowers first. The four table arrangements took twenty minutes longer than planned, but nothing had to be taken apart and rebuilt. By closing time, several blue tags had creases from being touched so often.

Two weeks later, a new colleague came over with a table-order sheet and asked which bucket could spare five white stems. Xu Lan checked the blue tag first, then felt how open the flower heads were, and finally took five stems from the bucket farthest inside. A trolley came from behind; she moved only an empty bucket near her feet. When the colleague handed her the next blue tag, she pressed it against the rim before reaching for the flowers. Her old skills at reading flower condition and making space were still there, but they no longer decided order assignment automatically.

One morning at the end of the month, three buckets of white tulips were again standing side by side under the worktable. Xu Lan passed with a trolley, her hand already lifting, then stopped at the first blue tag. She shifted the trolley half a step to the left. None of the three buckets moved.
storyParagraphsZh: 周一早上七点，许岚第一天到婚礼花艺工作室，九点前要完成四桌宴会花。她在批发花市做了十二年，最擅长在拥挤过道里一眼判断哪桶该补、哪束该先出。可她刚把三桶白郁金香并到一起，主花艺师就把其中两桶拉开：颜色一样，蓝签上的客户和桌号却不同，茎长也故意留得不一样。
许岚重新读了三张蓝签，还当面复述了“同色也不能并单”。十几分钟后，电话响起，送货推车正好堵在过道，两束快开的洋牡丹挡在前面。她一边接电话，一边已经把那两束移到最靠门的位置——在旧花市里，这样既能让推车过去，也能让快开的花先出货。等同事来找下午的新娘手捧花，其中一束已和另一单混在一起，大家花了十五分钟重新配齐枝材。
上午第二辆推车进来时，许岚又先让出过道，这次动作很有效：司机顺利通过，还说她“很会腾位置”。可她顺手把旁边一桶快开的白花也往前挪，转身才发现蓝签朝里，差点再次并进最近的一单。她把蓝签翻到外侧，第一次把“给推车让路”和“花材归哪张订单”拆成两个不同动作。
第二天，她给自己留了个小动作：每次取花前先碰一下蓝签。上午仍有两次手已经朝同色花桶递过去，碰到塑料签才改方向；下午推车经过时，她只挪空桶和通道，不先动订单花。四桌花比计划多用了二十分钟，却没有再拆开重配。收工时，几张蓝签已被她摸得起了折痕。
两周后，新人拿着一张桌花订单问哪桶白花能补五枝。许岚先看蓝签，再摸花头开放程度，最后从最里面那桶抽出五枝。推车从身后过来，她只移开脚边空桶；新人递来下一张蓝签，她先把签压在桶沿，再伸手。判断开放程度、腾通道这些旧本事仍在，只是不再自动决定花材归属。
月底的一个早晨，三桶白郁金香又并排放在操作台下。许岚推车经过，手已经抬起，却停在第一张蓝签上。她把推车向左让了半步，三只桶一只没动。
explanationParagraphs: Habitus refers to bodily dispositions, ways of judging, and a practical sense that accumulate through long experience in a social environment, allowing action without constant rule-by-rule calculation. These dispositions are durable and transferable, but not rigid scripts.

When people enter a different field, old dispositions can misfit. Repeated practice and new feedback can gradually reshape them. Habitus is not simply carelessness, personality, or memorizing the wrong procedure.
explanationParagraphsZh: 惯习是长期社会环境沉积成的身体倾向、判断方式和实践感，使人无需逐条计算也能生成行动。它持久且可迁移，但不是死规矩。
进入不同场域后，旧倾向可能失配；反复实践与新反馈又会慢慢改造它。惯习不是粗心、性格或背错流程。
articles.overall: Xu Lan clearly understands the blue-tag system, so the problem is not lack of training. The ways she learned to clear paths, move fast-opening flowers forward, and combine stock had once been flexible and effective in the wholesale market. In a studio organized around client-specific orders, some of those actions still help while others misfit the new boundaries. The fifteen-minute re-sort and the twenty extra minutes on the second day make the adjustment cost visible, while the unmoved three buckets at month-end show change emerging through repeated practice rather than one verbal instruction.
articles.overallZh: 许岚已经明确理解蓝签，所以问题不是培训不足。她在花市形成的让路、前移、归桶判断过去曾灵活而有效；进入按客户订单组织的工作室后，其中一部分动作仍有用，另一部分却因新场域的订单边界而失配。十五分钟重配和之后多用二十分钟显示调整有成本，而月底三桶花未被移动说明变化来自反复实践，不是一次口头提醒。

module.intro: A long-term environment can settle judgment into the body, allowing action without rule-by-rule calculation. In a new field, some dispositions still work while others misfit and slowly reorganize through repeated practice.
module.diagramTitle: How long-formed practical dispositions can misfit and adjust in a new field
diagramSteps: A long-term environment forms bodily tendencies that do not require constant calculation
Those tendencies were once flexibly effective in the familiar field
In a new field, the body still acts first on old cues
New task boundaries make some of those tendencies misfit
Repeated practice and feedback gradually reorganize action
diagramStepNotes: Twelve years in the wholesale market made clearing aisles, moving flowers forward, and grouping stock into practical judgments rather than memorized rules.
Clearing the path for the second trolley still works well, ruling out the idea that all of her old experience is simply wrong.
Xu Lan can already repeat the blue-tag rule, yet still moves the flowers first when the phone and trolley arrive together, so the problem is not merely lack of instruction.
The fifteen-minute re-sort and the extra twenty minutes the next day make the cost of misfit and adjustment visible.
Two weeks later, she still reads flower condition and makes room for trolleys, but checks the blue tag before assigning flowers to an order, showing gradual reshaping through practice.
mapping: Twelve years in the wholesale flower market → the historical source of embodied practical judgment.
Making way for the trolley still works → old dispositions can transfer without being simply wrong.
Moving fast-opening flowers forward and mixing an order → the same disposition misfitting a new field.
Repeatedly touching the blue tag → new feedback entering bodily action.
Three buckets left unmoved at month-end → practical dispositions have begun to reorganize.
module.boundary: Habitus is not fixed personality, a bad work habit, an explicit etiquette list, or an unchangeable fate, and not every skilled action should be called habitus. It refers to durable practical dispositions formed in a long-term social environment and expressed in relation to the cues and rewards of a particular field. The people and studio in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why can the same practical judgment Xu Lan brings from the wholesale market remain useful in one part of the new studio while another part has to change through repeated practice?

moduleZh.intro: 长期环境把判断沉进身体，使人无需逐条计算也能行动。进入新场域后，有些倾向仍有效，有些则会失配，并在反复实践中缓慢重组。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 长期形成的实践倾向怎样在新场域中失配并调整
diagramSteps: 长期环境形成无需逐条计算的身体倾向
旧倾向在熟悉场域中曾灵活有效
进入新场域后身体仍先沿旧线索行动
新任务边界让部分倾向出现失配
反复实践与反馈逐步重组行动方式
diagramStepNotes: 十二年花市经验让让路、前移和归桶成为实践判断，而非一条死背的规则。
给第二辆推车腾出通道仍然有效，排除了“旧经验全部错误”的解释。
许岚已能复述蓝签要求，却仍在电话和推车同时出现时先移动花，说明问题不只是没学会流程。
十五分钟重配与随后多用二十分钟，是旧倾向在新场域中失配和调整的具体代价。
两周后她仍使用判断花材状态和让路的经验，却先看蓝签再决定归属，显示惯习会被反复实践缓慢改造。
mapping: 十二年批发花市 → 身体化实践感的历史来源。
给推车让路仍有效 → 旧倾向具有可迁移性而非纯粹错误。
快开前移后混单 → 同一倾向进入新场域后的失配。
蓝签被反复触碰 → 新反馈进入身体动作的过程。
月底三桶花未被并动 → 实践倾向已开始重新组合。
moduleZh.boundary: 惯习不是固定性格、职业坏习惯、显性礼仪清单或无法改变的命运，也不能把所有熟练动作都叫作惯习。它指长期社会环境形成的持久实践倾向，与具体场域的线索和回报共同生成行动。本故事中的人物和工作室均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么同样是许岚从花市带来的身体判断，有的在新工作室里仍然有效，有的却必须经过反复实践才慢慢改变？

references.citation: Bourdieu, Pierre. *Outline of a Theory of Practice*. Translated by Richard Nice. Cambridge University Press, 1977.
references.use: Used to support habitus as a generative mediation between objective structures and practice, producing action through durable, transferable dispositions without requiring rule-by-rule instruction or continuous calculation.

references.citation: Bourdieu, Pierre. *The Logic of Practice*. Translated by Richard Nice. Stanford University Press, 1990.
references.use: Used to support practical sense, embodied history, and the relation between habitus and field, including the idea that habitus is not a rigid script and may lag behind or misfit a changed situation.

referencesZh.citation: Bourdieu, Pierre. *Outline of a Theory of Practice*. Translated by Richard Nice. Cambridge University Press, 1977.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持惯习作为客观结构与实践之间的生成性中介，以持久、可转移的倾向产生无需逐条规则或持续计算的行动。

referencesZh.citation: Bourdieu, Pierre. *The Logic of Practice*. Translated by Richard Nice. Stanford University Press, 1990.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持实践感、身体化历史与场域关系，以及惯习并非僵硬脚本，而是在具体处境中生成行动并可能出现迟滞或失配。

articles.title: The Ten-Minute Stall-Watching Sign
articles.summary: After Han Zhou turns ‘back in ten minutes’ into twenty-seven, neighboring vendors become more cautious about taking his sign. Soon even Lin Man, who keeps relaxing the limit for him, finds her own sign harder to pass on.
articles.summaryZh: 韩舟把“十分钟回来”拖成二十七分钟后，邻摊开始更谨慎地接他的牌。后来，就连一直替他放宽的林曼，也发现自己的牌没那么容易递出去了。
storyParagraphs: At 11:00 on Sunday, at the busiest point of the craft market, Han Zhou handed Lin Man at the next stall a small sign that read “Back in ten minutes” and asked her to watch his soap stall. No market manager required vendors to cover for one another. The six neighboring stalls had simply done it for two years: if someone needed the restroom or lunch, they passed the sign to a neighbor, who kept an eye on the stall for ten minutes.

Han Zhou was gone for twenty-seven minutes the first time. Lin Man took two payments for him and missed a customer at her own stall who wanted to order a custom bag. Han Zhou apologized when he returned and said the line had taken longer than expected. That afternoon, when he reached for the sign again, Zhao Qi pressed a hand over it. ‘Not today. I just had to help Lin Man make up for the customer she missed.’ Zhao Qi’s own stall was busy. Refusing this turn also gave him one less favor to ask of Han Zhou later, but he still did not hand over the sign.

The next week, Han Zhou brought lunch in advance but wanted to leave for fifteen minutes in the afternoon to collect a parcel. Lin Man thought he was trying to improve, so she took the sign and did not remind him about ten minutes. Han Zhou returned after twelve minutes, and nothing went wrong. But later, when Lin Man needed the restroom and offered the sign to the vendor on her other side, the vendor did not take it immediately. “How long this time?” they asked. Lin Man said ten minutes, and only then did the other person reach for the sign. For the first time, Lin Man saw that relaxing the expectation for Han Zhou was also changing how others treated her own requests.

Another Sunday, all six stalls were busy. Han Zhou offered the sign to Zhao Qi, who checked his phone and said he had to switch shifts in twelve minutes, so Han Zhou should ask someone else. Another vendor accepted it only after asking, ‘What time will you be back?’ Lin Man started to say, ‘He’s been quick lately,’ but A Ying, who sold jewellery, put down the cord she was knotting. ‘If it means anything whenever you feel like it, the sign might as well not say ten minutes.’ She had never watched Han Zhou’s stall, but over the previous two weeks two people had stopped her during the rush to ask what ten minutes now meant. When she picked up the cord again, the customer in front of her had moved to the earrings next door.

In the third week, Han Zhou picked up the sign again and said first, “I’ll be back before 11:42.” Zhao Qi took it. Han Zhou was back at 11:40 and then watched Zhao Qi’s stall for seven minutes. Later, a new vendor asked whether this was an official market rule. Lin Man said it was not in the handbook. But when the newcomer took the sign for the first time, they still checked the time on their phone.

Before closing, the laminated sign returned to the hook between the stalls, its edges worn pale. It still carried only the five Chinese characters meaning ‘Back in ten minutes.’ There was no signature line and no place to record a fine. A gust of wind made one corner tap twice against the hook.
storyParagraphsZh: 周日上午十一点，手作市集最忙的时候，韩舟把一张写着“十分钟回来”的小牌递给隔壁林曼，请她代看香皂摊。这个市集没有经理规定摊主必须互相看摊；只是六个相邻摊位两年来都这么做，谁去洗手间或拿午饭，就把牌交给邻摊，对方顺手照看十分钟。
韩舟第一次出去二十七分钟。林曼替他收了两笔款，又错过自己摊上一位想订定制包的客人。韩舟回来后连声道歉，说排队比预想长。午后他再次伸手拿牌时，赵启把牌按住：“今天先别了，我刚才替林曼补她漏掉的客人。”赵启自己的摊正忙，拒绝这次代看，也意味着他下次少一次向韩舟开口的余地；他仍没把牌递出去。
下一周韩舟提前带了午饭，下午又想离开十五分钟去取快递。林曼觉得他已经在改，便接过牌，也没提醒十分钟。韩舟十二分钟就回来，没有造成新损失。可傍晚林曼想去洗手间，把牌递给另一边，那位摊主没有马上接，只问：“你这次多久？”林曼说十分钟，对方才伸手。林曼第一次发现，自己替韩舟放宽也开始影响别人怎样接她的牌。
再过一个周日，六个摊位都忙起来。韩舟朝赵启递牌，赵启先看手机，说自己十二分钟后要交班，让他换个人；另一位摊主接下时直接问“几点回来”。林曼想替韩舟说“他最近都很快”，卖首饰的阿莹却放下正在打结的线：“你要是每次都说算了，牌上干脆别写十分钟。”她从没替韩舟守过摊，只是这两周已有两个人在最忙时追问她，十分钟到底算多久。等她重新拿起线，面前的客人已经去看隔壁的耳环。
第三周韩舟再拿牌时，自己先说：“十一点四十二前回来。”赵启接了。十一点四十，韩舟已经回到摊位，还顺手替赵启看了七分钟。后来一个新摊主问这是不是市集规定，林曼说管理手册里没有；可那人第一次接牌时，还是先看了一眼手机上的时间。
收市前，那张塑封小牌回到中间的挂钩上，边角已经磨白。牌面只写着五个字：“十分钟回来。”旁边没有签名，也没有罚款栏。风一吹，牌角轻轻碰了两下挂钩。
explanationParagraphs: Group norms can persist through approval, reminders, distancing, reputational changes, and other distributed sanctions. Members do not only expect others to comply; they also expect deviations to carry some cost.

Norm enforcement can also place pressure on people who repeatedly fail to enforce the norm. It differs from formal law, ordinary habit, or direct reciprocity because the shared expectation itself is maintained through peer action.
explanationParagraphsZh: 群体规范会通过成员的赞许、提醒、疏远、声誉变化或其他分散制裁持续。成员不仅预期别人遵守，也预期偏离者会付出代价。
规范执行还可能包含对不执行者的压力。它不同于正式法律、普通习惯或单纯互惠；关键是共同期待本身被同伴行动维持。
articles.overall: The ten-minute stall-watching practice is not a formal order and is not merely direct reciprocity in the sense of “people stop helping whoever takes advantage.” After Han Zhou’s overrun, even vendors who were not directly harmed remind others, refuse, or raise the conditions for taking the sign. When Lin Man repeatedly relaxes the expectation, her own access to cooperation also tightens. These sanctions carry small costs but still occur, helping preserve the shared expectation. Cooperation gradually recovers only after Han Zhou starts stating 11:42 and returning at 11:40.
articles.overallZh: 十分钟代看不是正式命令，也不只是“谁占便宜就没人帮谁”的直接互惠。韩舟超时后，同伴即使没有直接受损，也会提醒、拒绝或提高接牌条件；林曼持续放宽时，她自己的合作机会也开始收紧。这样的制裁有小成本，却仍发生，使共同期待得以延续。韩舟主动报11:42并在11:40回来后，互助才逐渐恢复。

module.intro: A social norm persists through shared expectations and distributed peer responses. Deviators face cooperation costs, and people who repeatedly excuse them may also face pressure, which distinguishes a norm from ordinary habit or direct reciprocity.
module.diagramTitle: How distributed sanctions and pressure on non-enforcers sustain a norm
diagramSteps: A group develops a predictable shared standard of behavior
A deviation imposes a real coordination cost on others
Peers respond with small, distributed sanctions
People who repeatedly fail to enforce the norm also face cooperation pressure
When behavior realigns, the shared expectation gradually recovers
diagramStepNotes: The ten-minute practice is not ordered by a manager, yet it has long organized short absences across six stalls.
Han Zhou’s twenty-seven-minute absence causes Lin Man to miss a custom-bag order, giving the deviation a clear real cost.
When Zhao Qi refuses another high-traffic favor, he also gives up a small opportunity for reciprocal help, showing that enforcement is not completely costless.
A vendor who never watched Han Zhou’s stall still reminds Lin Man, while Lin Man’s own requests draw extra scrutiny, showing pressure extending to someone who repeatedly relaxes the norm.
Han Zhou states 11:42 and returns at 11:40; keeping the commitment changes what others expect the next time he hands over the sign.
mapping: The worn ten-minute sign → the stable visible carrier of the shared expectation.
The twenty-seven-minute absence and missed order → the deviation and its real cost.
Zhao Qi refusing another turn → distributed peer sanction.
Lin Man’s own request being questioned → pressure on someone who repeatedly fails to enforce the norm.
The 11:42 promise and 11:40 return → behavior realigning and cooperation recovering.
module.boundary: Norm enforcement is not the same as formal law, a manager’s order, personal morality, ordinary reciprocity, or bullying. Norms may be useful, inefficient, or unfair, and sanctions may become excessive. This story shows only how one low-intensity mutual-help norm persists through mutual expectations, distributed sanctions, and pressure on those who fail to enforce it. The people and market are fictional.
module.reflection: Why would someone who has never watched Han Zhou’s stall still remind Lin Man not to keep stretching the ten-minute expectation, and how is that different from simply calculating whether they personally will lose out?

moduleZh.intro: 社会规范靠共同期待和分散的同伴回应持续。偏离者会付出合作代价，持续替偏离者放宽的人也可能受到压力，因此规范不同于普通习惯或直接互惠。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 分散制裁与对未执行者的压力怎样维持规范
diagramSteps: 群体先形成可预期的共同行为标准
偏离给他人带来真实协作成本
同伴以分散的小制裁回应偏离
持续不执行规范者也承受合作压力
行为重新对齐后共同期待逐步恢复
diagramStepNotes: 十分钟代看没有经理命令，却长期组织六个摊位的短暂离开。
韩舟二十七分钟未归让林曼错失定制订单，偏离产生明确成本。
赵启拒绝高峰代看时自己也放弃一次互助机会，说明执行并非完全无成本。
未直接替韩舟守摊的人也提醒林曼，且林曼自己的请求被多问一步，显示压力延伸到持续放宽者。
韩舟报11:42并在11:40回来，按时行为改变别人下一次接牌的预期。
mapping: 磨白的十分钟小牌 → 群体共同期待的稳定载体。
二十七分钟离开与错失订单 → 偏离及其现实代价。
赵启拒绝再次接牌 → 分散同伴制裁。
林曼的请求也被追问 → 对持续不执行者的压力。
11:42承诺与11:40返回 → 行为重新对齐后合作恢复。
moduleZh.boundary: 规范执行不等于正式法律、老板命令、个人道德、普通互惠或霸凌。规范可能有益、低效甚至不公，制裁也可能过强。本故事只展示一个低强度互助规范如何通过相互期待、分散制裁和对未执行者的压力持续；人物和市集均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么一个从未替韩舟守过摊的人仍会提醒林曼别把十分钟继续放宽，而这种提醒与单纯计算自己会不会吃亏有什么不同？

references.citation: Axelrod, Robert. “An Evolutionary Approach to Norms.” *American Political Science Review* 80, no. 4 (1986): 1095–1111.
references.use: Used to support the idea that norms can remain stable in groups without a central authority through sanctions, including the role of meta-norms in sanctioning those who fail to enforce the norm.

references.citation: Bicchieri, Cristina. *The Grammar of Society: The Nature and Dynamics of Social Norms*. Cambridge University Press, 2006.
references.use: Used to support the idea that social norms are sustained by empirical expectations, normative expectations, and conditional compliance, and that inefficient norms may persist while changing a norm requires changing mutual expectations rather than only individual preferences.

referencesZh.citation: Axelrod, Robert. “An Evolutionary Approach to Norms.” *American Political Science Review* 80, no. 4 (1986): 1095–1111.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持规范可在没有中央权威的群体中通过制裁而稳定，也支持“元规范”——惩罚那些没有执行规范的人——如何进一步维持共同规则。

referencesZh.citation: Bicchieri, Cristina. *The Grammar of Society: The Nature and Dynamics of Social Norms*. Cambridge University Press, 2006.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持社会规范由经验期待、规范期待与条件性遵从共同维持，也支持低效规范可能持续、改变规范需要改变相互期待而非只改变个体偏好。

articles.title: The Fourteen-Second Video
articles.summary: A fourteen-second video says a mall ceiling has collapsed and people are injured. With less than an hour to deadline, Su Yao finds that the footage is real, but the sentence may not be.
articles.summaryZh: 一段十四秒视频写着“天花板坍塌，已经有人受伤”。离截稿不到一小时，苏遥发现画面是真的，那句话却未必是。
storyParagraphs: At 17:12, community reporter Su Yao received a fourteen-second video. People on the mall’s ground floor were moving quickly toward the exits; the camera jerked, and a cloud of white dust fell in the distance. The forwarded caption said, “The ceiling has collapsed and people have been injured.” She had to decide before 18:00 whether to publish a breaking update. She pasted the sentence into the headline field and left the cursor blinking after the words “ceiling collapse.”

The earliest uploader quickly sent her the original file. Its timestamp was 17:03, and the shop signs in the frame matched the mall’s north side. The person who filmed it said he had been standing by the second-floor escalator. He had seen security staff directing people out and had seen the white dust fall, but he had not seen a ceiling come down or anyone injured. He had heard someone nearby shout that there had been a collapse. Su Yao deleted “people have been injured” from the headline and added a separate note: “Seen firsthand: evacuation, dust.”

A little after 17:20, the mall duty desk said the 17:02 evacuation might be connected to a dust alarm in the renovation area. The fire-safety inspector on shift confirmed the evacuation time but would say only that no report of a structural collapse had reached him. Su Yao pasted the two replies into separate notes and moved neither into the headline. She marked ‘collapse’ as unverified and asked a colleague to complete the timeline from outside the mall.

Her colleague found public footage from the street on the north side: at 17:05, two ambulances passed but did not stop at the mall. Then a construction notice arrived in Su Yao’s inbox stating that after 17:00 workers would be removing a plasterboard partition in an empty unit on the north side. She dragged the fourteen-second video back to its 17:03 frame; the white dust appeared close to the construction barrier. By then she had removed “ceiling collapse” from any publishable headline, but she still did not replace it with the definitive claim that the dust was “only construction dust.”

At 17:47, the fire department issued its first briefing: demolition work in the renovation area had triggered a detector and the mall had briefly evacuated; an on-site inspection found no structural collapse, and no injuries had been reported. Su Yao used the briefing to add the inspection result that had previously been missing, but she still wrote “no structural collapse found” and “no injuries reported.” She also kept one sentence stating that the source of the white dust in the video had not been independently confirmed by the reporter.

At 18:02, the update went live. In the editor’s version history, the earliest draft still showed the deleted words “ceiling collapse.” Su Yao saved the original video, the 17:03 screenshot, the 17:02 evacuation record, the 17:05 street footage, the construction notice, and the 17:47 fire briefing in the reporting folder. She added “v1” to the end of the filename.
storyParagraphsZh: 下午五点十二分，社区记者苏遥收到一段十四秒视频：商场一楼有人快步往出口走，镜头一晃，远处落下一片白色粉尘，转发文字写着“天花板坍塌，已经有人受伤”。晚六点前她要决定是否发快讯。她先把这句话贴进标题框，光标停在“坍塌”两个字后面。
最早上传者很快发来原文件。时间是17:03，画面里的店铺招牌能对上商场北侧；拍摄者说自己站在二楼扶梯口，只看到保安让人往外走和白色粉尘落下，“坍塌”是听旁边人喊的，伤者也没亲眼见到。苏遥把“已经有人受伤”从标题删掉，又在笔记里把“亲见：疏散、粉尘”单独写了一行。
五点二十几分，商场值班台说17:02的疏散可能与装修区粉尘报警有关；当班消防巡查员也确认了疏散时间，却只肯说自己没有接到结构坍塌报告。苏遥把两句回复分别贴进笔记，没有移进标题。她将第一版里的“坍塌”标成待核，又让同事从商场外面补齐17:02之后的时间线。
同事调来北侧街口公开视频：17:05有两辆救护车经过，却没有停在商场门口。随后一张施工通知发到苏遥邮箱，写着北侧空铺17:00后拆石膏板隔墙。她把十四秒视频拖回17:03那一帧，白色粉尘正靠近围挡。到这时，她已经把“天花板坍塌”从可发标题中拿掉，但仍没有把“只是装修粉尘”写成确定事实。
17:47，消防部门才发出第一条简报：装修区拆除时粉尘触发探测器，商场短时疏散；现场检查未发现结构坍塌，暂无人员受伤报告。苏遥用这条材料补上此前缺失的现场检查结果，却仍把正文写成“未发现”和“暂无报告”，并保留一句：视频中的白色粉尘来源尚未由记者独立确认。
18:02，快讯上线。编辑器历史版本里，最早那一栏还留着被删掉的“天花板坍塌”。苏遥把原视频、17:03截图、17:02疏散记录、17:05街口视频、施工通知和17:47消防简报一起存进报道文件夹，文件名最后加了“v1”。
explanationParagraphs: News verification tests a specific claim through a reviewable process: trace original sources, limit each source to what it actually encountered, check time and place, seek independent evidence and alternative explanations, and match the strength of the report to the strength of the evidence.

Verification is not simply waiting for an authoritative answer, and it does not guarantee absolute certainty. The key is to separate what is known, inferred, and unknown, then update or correct the report as evidence changes.
explanationParagraphsZh: 新闻核实是用可复查过程检验具体主张：追原始来源，限定来源实际接触范围，核对时地，寻找独立证据和替代解释，并让报道强度匹配证据。
核实不等于等待一个权威答案，也不保证绝对确定。关键是区分已知、推断与未知，并随证据更新或更正。
articles.overall: The 17:47 fire briefing is not the single authoritative answer that overturns the rumor. Before it appears, Su Yao has already weakened the headline using the 17:03 original file, the filming location, the 17:02 evacuation information, the 17:05 street footage, and the post-17:00 construction notice. The briefing adds an on-site inspection result, but even then she writes only “no structural collapse found” and “no injuries reported,” rather than converting remaining uncertainty into certainty.
articles.overallZh: 17:47消防简报不是推翻传闻的唯一答案。苏遥在它出现前，已经用17:03原文件、拍摄位置、17:02疏散信息、17:05街口视频和17:00施工通知逐步删弱标题；简报只是进一步补入现场检查结果。即使如此，她仍只写“未发现”“暂无报告”，没有把未知改写成绝对确定。

module.intro: Authentic material may support only part of a claim. Journalistic verification asks what a source actually witnessed, whether time and place match, and what independent evidence or alternative explanations remain, then matches the wording to the evidence.
module.diagramTitle: How a breaking claim narrows as reviewable evidence accumulates
diagramSteps: Trace the claim back to the earliest publisher and obtain the original file
Limit the source to what it actually encountered
Check whether time, place, and content correspond
Use independent material to test alternative explanations
Rewrite to match the evidence and preserve what remains unknown
diagramStepNotes: The 17:03 original file and north-side shop signs establish time and place, but directly show only evacuation and dust.
The filmer did not witness a collapse or injuries, so the two stronger claims in the forwarded caption are separated from what he actually saw.
The 17:02 evacuation record and 17:05 street footage add distinct points to the timeline but do not determine the cause on their own.
The post-17:00 construction notice makes renovation dust a plausible alternative explanation, but not a conclusion before 17:47.
The fire briefing provides an inspection result, yet the final article still uses “no structural collapse found” and “no injuries reported,” preserving the evidentiary boundary.
mapping: The fourteen-second original video → reviewable original material with a limited information range.
Successive edits in the headline field → the strength of the report changes with the evidence.
17:02, 17:03, and 17:05 → timeline verification.
The post-17:00 construction notice and the 17:47 fire briefing → independent material constraining an alternative explanation and the on-site conclusion.
The filename “v1” → the report remains open to updating as new evidence arrives.
module.boundary: Verification does not mean that only firsthand observation is credible, nor does it require absolute certainty. Honest eyewitnesses, mall staff, and fire officials may each know only part of an event, and multiple sources may share the same mistaken origin. What matters is a reviewable method, the limits of each source’s access, independent evidence, alternative explanations, and explicit uncertainty. The mall, reporter, and event in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why is the 17:47 fire briefing important while still being only the final piece in Su Yao’s verification chain rather than an authoritative answer that replaces all earlier checking?

moduleZh.intro: 真实材料也可能只支持一项断言的一部分。新闻核实追问来源看见了什么、时间地点能否对上、还有哪些独立线索和替代解释，再让措辞强度服从当前证据。

moduleZh.boundary: 核实不等于只有亲眼所见才可信，也不等于最终必须达到绝对确定。诚实目击者、商场和消防都可能只掌握事件的一部分；多个来源也可能共享同一错误起点。关键是可复查方法、来源接触范围、独立证据、替代解释和明确限制。故事中的商场、记者与事件均为虚构。

articles.title: The Third Question Card Beside the Coffee Machine
articles.summary: Before the public Q&A, Lin Zhen writes a question card for the clinic and another for drainage repairs. Each morning she turns through the weekly beside her coffee machine.
storyParagraphs: At the beginning of September, Lin Zhen sits behind the counter of her café writing question cards for a public Q&A at the library. The community clinic her mother uses is being renovated, so her first card asks, “When will the temporary entrance be removed?” The second concerns repairs to the drainage channel behind the shop. Two late-shift employees have long had to cycle or carpool after finishing at 22:30 because the last bus does not connect with their shift. Lin Zhen knows this, but she has never put it on the list of issues she plans to raise at the meeting.

That week, the front page of the Hexi Weekly covers late-night buses, using four weeks of timetable data and interviews with night-shift passengers. In the second week, the bus figures are broadly similar to the week before, yet the front page again carries a service piece about options after the last bus. In the third week, a route map for services after 22:00 takes up a large part of the front page. The clinic and drainage work also receive updates, but on inside pages.

Lin Zhen glances through the front page while opening the café each day. In the first week, she simply folds the paper and leaves it beside the coffee machine. While preparing Friday’s rota in the second week, she sees the last-bus story again and looks back at the “bike” and “carpool” notes her employees have been writing beside their shifts for several weeks. When the route map appears in the third week, she cuts it out, clips it into the rota folder, and writes a third question card: “Can the existing night routes connect with shifts ending after 22:30?”

Her mother calls to ask again whether someone will show her the way at the clinic’s temporary entrance. Lin Zhen finds the contractor’s earlier text and adds its date and time to the back of the first card. She also prints the drainage photograph from the residents’ group and attaches it to the second. Before leaving, she puts both cards and the new bus question in a clear folder. The “bike” and “carpool” notes in the rota have accumulated in different colors of ink; the clipped route map sits behind that same page.

In the fourth week, question cards cover a long table at the library. The bakery owner beside Lin Zhen has written “late-night buses,” adding a question about the cost of extra departures. Hearing him, a night-shift worker takes a pen and asks on her own card whether the existing last departure could simply be moved later. A staff member groups the bus cards together. Clinic and drainage cards lie elsewhere on the table, waiting for the relevant departments to answer.

After the session, Lin Zhen slips her three cards back into the café’s clear folder. The next morning, the clinic card is still in front, the bus card sits behind the staff rota, and the clipped route map remains beside the coffee machine. The new issue of the weekly has already switched its front page to the clinic renovation.
articles.overall: Agenda-setting concerns how repeated selection and prominent placement in the media influence which issues enter public attention and discussion. Greater attention to an issue can coexist with disagreement about how to address it.
explanationParagraphs: The late-shift connection problem already exists, and the bus data do not suddenly worsen. What changes across three weeks of front-page coverage is how often Lin Zhen revisits an existing problem and eventually adds it to her formal question list.

The clinic remains her main concern, the residents’ group supplies drainage information, and people raising buses disagree. The visible change is the known bus problem entering formal discussion. Its relative ranking is not measured, and media coverage cannot be identified as the sole cause.

module.intro: Observe whether an issue receives more attention, checking, and discussion after repeated prominent coverage.
module.diagramTitle: How an Old Problem Becomes the Third Formal Question Card
diagramSteps: Record the person’s existing priorities and a known issue not yet on the list
Give the same issue repeated prominent coverage
Let repeated exposure prompt renewed attention to existing everyday records
Add the issue to the formal question list without displacing all earlier priorities
The issue appears in public questions while specific positions remain different
diagramStepNotes: Lin Zhen first writes clinic and drainage cards; she already knows her employees have late-bus problems.
Buses occupy the front page for three weeks while the underlying timetable facts remain broadly stable.
She revisits the long-standing bike and carpool notes in the staff rota.
Buses become the third card, while the clinic remains first.
At the Q&A, several people raise buses but focus on cost, timing, and other different concerns.
mapping: Old “bike/carpool” notes on the rota → evidence that the problem already existed.
Three consecutive front pages → repeated source of issue salience.
Clipped route map → the media issue entering everyday decision materials.
Three question cards → the known bus problem enters formal discussion while earlier concerns remain.
module.boundary: Agenda-setting does not mean that media coverage single-handedly creates demand or persuades audiences to support one policy position. Personal experience, real-world changes, other media, and social information sources all affect issue importance; a fictional story can illustrate a possible mechanism but cannot prove a unique causal effect.
module.reflection: When a known problem enters a formal question list, what evidence would you examine to distinguish possible contributions from coverage, personal experience, and changing facts?

references.use: Supports the original research framework linking issue selection, repetition, and salience with audience perceptions of issue importance; the story is not a replication of the original study and is not used to prove one-way causation.

references.use: McCombs’s review of agenda-setting research across its past, present, and future, for further reading.

articles.titleZh: 咖啡机旁的第三张问题卡
articles.summaryZh: 问答会前，林真给诊所和排水各写一张问题卡。咖啡机旁的周报，她每天早上都会翻一遍。
storyParagraphsZh: 九月初，林真在咖啡店柜台后写图书馆公开问答会的问题卡。她母亲常去的社区诊所正在改造，所以第一张写“临时入口什么时候撤”；第二张是店后巷的雨水沟维修。店里两名晚班员工早就常在二十二点半下班后改骑车或拼车，因为末班公交接不上，林真知道这件事，却一直没把它列进要带到问答会的问题。
那周《河西周报》首页做晚班公交：记者用了连续四周的班次表和夜班乘客采访。第二周，班次数据和前周大致一样，首页仍是一篇末班车服务稿；第三周，晚十点后的线路图又占了首页大块位置。诊所和排水也有更新，但都在内页。
林真每天开店会顺手翻首页。第一周她只是把报纸折回咖啡机旁；第二周做周五排班时，她又看见末班车那篇，把员工过去几周写在班表边的“骑车”“拼车”标记重新看了一遍。第三周的线路图出来后，她剪下那一块，夹进排班夹，才写了第三张问题卡：“现有夜班线路能不能接上十点半后的下班时间？”
母亲打来电话，又问诊所的临时入口有没有人指路。林真把施工方先前发来的短信找出来，在第一张卡背面补了时间。居民群里的雨水沟照片，她也打印一张贴到第二张卡上。出门前，她把这两张和新写的公交卡装进透明夹；排班夹里那几处“骑车”“拼车”的笔迹已经用了不同颜色，剪下的线路图夹在同一页后面。
第四周，图书馆长桌上铺开问题卡。林真旁边的烘焙店老板也写了“晚班公交”，在下面补问增加班次要花多少钱。一位夜班员工听到这话，拿过笔，在自己的卡上写能否只调整现有末班车的时间。工作人员将几张公交卡放在一起，诊所和排水的卡另放在桌面上，等待各部门的人来答。
散场后，林真把自己的三张卡塞回店里的透明夹。第二天早上，诊所卡仍放在最前面，公交卡夹在员工排班表后，剪下的线路图压在咖啡机旁。新一期周报首页已经换成诊所施工进度。
articles.overallZh: 议程设置关注媒体怎样通过持续选择、重复和显著位置，影响哪些问题更容易进入公众注意与讨论。一个议题受到更多关注时，人们对解决方案仍可能意见不同。
explanationParagraphsZh: 晚班接驳问题早已存在，公交数据也没有突然恶化；连续三周首页报道改变的是林真重新查看既有问题的频率，并最终把公交加入正式提问清单。
诊所仍是她首要关切，居民群也提供排水信息；提公交的人意见不同。可见变化是已知公交问题进入正式讨论，未测出它相对其他议题的排序幅度，也不能据此认定媒体是唯一原因。

moduleZh.intro: 观察一个议题被反复突出后，是否更常被看见、查阅和带入讨论。

公交连续三周占首页，班次事实大致稳定。
她重新查看班表上长期存在的骑车、拼车标记。

articles.title: How Many Homes Were Still Cold?
articles.summary: After the same heating repair, property management says 7 homes remain, the contractor reports 92% completion, and 11 residents still report cold rooms. None of the three sheets is false, yet they cannot become the same answer.
articles.summaryZh: 同一次供暖维修，物业说只剩7户，维修公司说完成92%，回访却有11户仍冷。三张纸都没撒谎，却不能写成同一个答案。
storyParagraphs: On Monday afternoon, community editor Zhou Ji stood in a resident’s living room in Building 3. The radiator was slightly warm across the top and still cold below. The resident handed him a phone showing a message circulating in the owners’ chat: “At least half the households still have no heat.” Property management, however, had sent him the figure “7 open work orders,” while the repair company said “92% completion.” With the evening edition closing at 17:30, he had to decide which way the headline should go.

Back at the newsroom, Zhou Ji spread out the property-management work-order sheet. Seven homes were indeed marked “open,” but more than ten entries marked “completed” carried the note “resident not home, awaiting recheck.” He called the Building 3 resident he had just visited. The resident said the system showed “completed,” while the living room was still cold. The sheet made Zhou Ji drop the headline “Only 7 homes remain,” but it still told him which problems the administrative system had not yet closed.

The repair company then sent outlet-temperature readings from the boiler room and pressure records from the main risers in each building. An engineer checked the Building 3 address and found that the main riser there was within normal parameters. He explained that 92% referred to repair tasks completed. Zhou Ji did not erase the cold living room, because the system-level readings could not see an individual radiator. But the wording “large-scale system failure continues” also became harder to support. On the second sheet, he wrote two separate headings: “system level” and “household level.”

Before 16:00, the residents’ committee delivered its callback sheet for 36 households. Eleven had said that morning that their homes still felt colder than usual. For a moment, that number pulled the headline back toward “the problem remains widespread,” until Zhou Ji noticed the callbacks had taken place from 08:00 to 10:00, while the repair company’s final venting round had ended at 10:30. He asked the committee to contact 6 of those households for an afternoon recheck. Only 2 were still clearly below normal, including the Building 3 home. The other 30 households had not been rechecked that afternoon, so those 6 could not stand in for the entire development either.

Zhou Ji laid the three sheets side by side and placed a different draft headline beneath each one. ‘Only 7 homes remain’ sat under the work-order sheet, but the sheet still contained ‘completed, awaiting recheck.’ ‘Large-scale system failure continues’ sat under the equipment readings, but Building 3's main riser was normal. ‘Fully restored’ sat under the callback sheet, but 2 homes were still cold that afternoon. He opened a new line and wrote, ‘Main heating system restored; a small number of homes still awaiting recheck,’ then returned 7, 92%, 11/36, and 2/6 to the article with their separate meanings.

At 17:28, the page was sent. The three sheets were still spread across the editor’s desk. Zhou Ji deleted the last occurrence of “large-scale” from the headline and crossed out “fully restored” in the alternative version. The Building 3 resident’s phone number was still tucked beneath the callback sheet, with one note beside it: “Ask again tomorrow morning.”
storyParagraphsZh: 周一下午，社区编辑周霁站在3号楼一户居民的客厅里，暖气片上半截微温，下半截仍凉。屋主把手机递给他，业主群里正转着一句话：“至少一半住户家里还不热。”物业发来的数字却是“未关闭工单7户”，维修公司则说“完成率92%”。晚报五点半截稿，他必须决定标题该往哪边写。
回编辑部后，周霁摊开物业工单表。七户确实标着“未关闭”，可十几条“已完成”后面写着“住户不在家，待复测”。他打电话给刚才那户，屋主说系统里显示“已完成”，客厅却还冷。工单表因此让他放弃“只剩7户”的标题，但它仍告诉他哪些问题在行政系统里尚未关闭。
维修公司随后发来锅炉房出口温度和各楼栋主立管压力记录。工程师查到3号楼主立管参数正常，并解释92%指维修任务完成率。周霁没有因此删掉那间冷客厅，因为这些参数看不到单户散热器；但“大面积系统仍坏着”的写法也开始站不住。他在第二张纸上把“系统层”和“单户层”分开写。
下午四点前，居民委员会送来36户回访表，其中11户说上午家里仍比平时冷。这个数字一度把标题又往“问题很大”拉回去，可周霁看见回访时间是8:00到10:00，维修公司的最后一轮排气却到10:30才结束。他让居委会帮忙联系其中6户下午复测，只有2户仍明显偏低，3号楼那户就是其中之一。其余30户没有下午复测，因此这6户也不能替全小区作结论。
周霁把三张纸并排压在桌上，又把三个备选标题各放在一张纸下面。“只剩7户”压在工单表下，可“已完成待复测”还在表里；“系统仍大面积故障”压在设备记录下，可3号楼主立管参数正常；“完全恢复”压在回访表下，可下午仍有2户偏低。他最后另起一行，写成“主系统已恢复，少数住户仍待复测”，再把7户、92%、11/36和2/6分别写回正文。
17:28，版面送出。编辑台上三张纸还摊着，周霁把标题里最后一个“大面积”删掉，又把备选标题中的“完全恢复”划掉。3号楼那户的电话号码还夹在回访表下面，旁边写着“明早再问”。
explanationParagraphs: Source triangulation tests the same claim using sources, records, or methods with genuinely different paths of access, interests, and failure modes. A larger number of sources is not the same as independence, and conclusions are not decided by majority vote.

Each line of evidence can be useful while retaining blind spots. Disagreement can expose differences in time, scope, unit, or definition, allowing several paths together to narrow, revise, or qualify a claim.
explanationParagraphsZh: 来源三角验证让接触路径、利益和失败方式不同的来源、资料或方法共同检验同一主张。数量本身不等于独立性，也不能靠多数票决定结论。
每条证据都可能有用又有盲区。分歧能暴露时间、范围、单位或定义差异，从而共同收窄、改写或限定主张。
articles.overall: The work orders, equipment measurements, morning callback, and afternoon rechecks all change Zhou Ji’s next judgment, yet none can finish the story alone. The work-order system misses “completed, awaiting recheck” cases; system measurements cannot see individual radiators; the morning callback comes before the 10:30 final venting; and the 6 afternoon rechecks cover only part of the 11 households that had reported being cold. The conclusion is therefore narrowed by several different evidence paths together, rather than determined by the Building 3 case, one number, or a single better sample.
articles.overallZh: 工单、设备测量、上午回访和下午复测都改变了周霁的下一步判断，却没有任何一条足够单独收尾：工单漏掉“已完成待复测”，设备参数看不到单户，上午回访早于10:30排气，下午6户复测又只覆盖11户中的一部分。结论因此由多条不同路径共同收窄，而不是由3号楼个案、某个数字或一次更好抽样单独决定。

module.intro: Source triangulation uses evidence with different access paths and blind spots to bound a claim. Agreement can strengthen a judgment, while disagreement reveals differences in timing, scope, and definition.
module.diagramTitle: How different evidence paths jointly constrain one claim
diagramSteps: Start with a disputed claim that needs testing
Bring in evidence that reaches the issue through different paths
Identify what each line of evidence can and cannot see
Use disagreement to locate differences in time, scope, and definition
Let several evidence paths jointly narrow the final claim
diagramStepNotes: The cold Building 3 living room proves that an individual problem exists, but cannot represent the whole development.
Work orders record administrative status but place some “completed, awaiting recheck” cases among closed items.
Main-riser readings reflect system-level operation but cannot observe every household radiator.
The 11/36 figure comes from callbacks before the 10:30 final venting; 2 of 6 afternoon rechecks remain cold, but those 6 are only a partial sample.
The final headline keeps both system recovery and a small number of unresolved households instead of letting any one source win.
mapping: The cold living room in Building 3 → a real case with limited power to generalize.
7 open work orders → an administrative-record path and its blind spot.
92% completion and main-riser readings → a technical-measurement path and its blind spot.
11/36, the 10:30 venting point, and 2 of 6 afternoon rechecks → a resident-outcome path constrained by time and sample range.
Deleting both “large-scale” and “fully restored” at 17:28 → several independent paths jointly change the scope of the claim.
module.boundary: Source triangulation is not mechanically finding three people who agree, and official, technical, or resident sources are not inherently more reliable. If several sources share the same origin, they may only be echoes; a larger sample also does not automatically replace other evidence paths. What matters is whether the paths of access, blind spots, and failure modes are genuinely different. The residential complex, people, and data in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why are the 6 afternoon rechecks highly useful while still being unable, by themselves, to replace the work orders, system measurements, and broader callback?

moduleZh.intro: 来源三角验证依靠接触路径和盲区不同的证据共同限定主张。相符之处可以增强判断，分歧则帮助发现时间、范围和定义差异。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 不同证据路径怎样共同限定一个主张
diagramSteps: 从具体争议提出待检验主张
引入接触路径不同的证据
确认每条证据能看见与看不见什么
用分歧定位时间、范围和定义差异
让多条证据共同收窄最终主张
diagramStepNotes: 3号楼冷客厅证明单户问题真实存在，却不能代表全小区。
工单能记录行政状态，却把“已完成待复测”放在关闭项中。
主立管参数反映系统层运行，却看不到每户散热器。
11/36来自10:30前回访；下午6户复测中2户仍冷，但这6户只是部分样本。
最终标题同时保留系统恢复与少数待复测，而不是让任何一条证据获胜。
mapping: 3号楼冷客厅 → 真实个案，但外推范围有限。
7户工单 → 行政记录路径及其盲区。
92%与主立管参数 → 技术测量路径及其盲区。
11/36、10:30、6户复测中2户 → 居民结果路径与时间范围限制。
17:28删掉两种极端标题 → 多条独立路径共同改变主张范围。
moduleZh.boundary: 来源三角验证不是机械找三个人赞同，也不意味着官方、技术或民间来源天然更可靠。多个来源若共享同一原点，只是回声；更大的样本也不自动取代其他证据路径。关键是接触路径、盲区和失败方式是否真正不同。故事中的小区、人物与数据均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么下午复测的6户非常有价值，却仍不能单独替代工单、系统参数和更大范围的回访？

articles.fieldTitleZh: 图书馆、信息与档案研究
articles.title: The Pencil Number on the Back of the Photograph
articles.summary: An authentic 1986 photograph already has a label calling its subjects the city's first female bus drivers. Two days before installation, TR-4/12 on the back makes Gu Xia pull the label out again.
articles.summaryZh: 一张1986年的真实照片已经配好“第一批女司机”展签。布展前两天，背后的TR-4/12让顾夏把展签又抽了出来。
storyParagraphs: On Wednesday afternoon, the community museum had only two days left before installation. In front of Gu Xia lay a 1986 black-and-white photograph showing six women in bus uniforms beside a vehicle door. Blue ink on the back said “first female drivers.” The aging paper, photo-lab mark, people, and street scene all matched the period. The old label draft—“The city’s first group of female bus drivers”—had already been printed and needed only to be placed in the display case.

As Gu Xia prepared to scan the photograph, she noticed a faint pencil number in one corner, partly covered by an old glue mark: ‘TR-4/12.’ The donation record said only ‘from the Chen family's belongings’ and did not say what the photograph had originally been stored with. The paper, people, and street scene still looked credible, but she put the old label draft back into the folder and turned to the accession list for the rest of the same donation.

The list connected TR-4 to a group titled “Spring 1986 Driver Training Publicity Materials.” Item 12 was the photograph in front of her. In neighboring photographs, the same six women appeared beside a simulated steering wheel and seated at classroom desks. A course schedule tucked into the publicity booklet read, “12 candidates; positions assigned after final assessment.” Gu Xia could now confirm that the six women were part of the training activity, but she still could not find a record showing that all six had formally entered service.

The next morning, she found a loan slip inside the donor’s father’s work notebook. The training center had once lent the TR-4 group to a bus-company publicity officer to produce recruitment posters, then received it back with the booklet. When the family later sorted the belongings, the photograph was placed by itself in an album while the publicity booklet went into another bag; after accessioning, the two were again placed in different boxes. The photograph itself had always remained genuine. What changed was its separation from the materials that had once made its use and context visible.

With only a few hours left before the gallery closed for installation, Gu Xia did not remove the photograph, and she did not treat TR-4/12 as proof that none of the six women ever became drivers. She rewrote the label: “Publicity photograph from a 1986 women’s bus-driver training course. Existing records confirm that all six women attended training; separate records are still needed to establish which later entered formal service.” She then relinked the scan to the publicity-booklet page, course schedule, loan slip, and donation batch while retaining the TR-4/12 identifier.

The night before installation, the photograph finally went into the display case. The TR-4/12 marking on the back was no longer visible, but a small line had been added to the lower-right corner of the new label: ‘Record relationship: TR-4/12, Training Publicity Materials group.’ Gu Xia placed the old label draft reading ‘The city’s first group of female bus drivers’ back into the folder.
storyParagraphsZh: 周三下午，社区博物馆只剩两天布展。顾夏面前是一张1986年的黑白照片：六名穿公交制服的女性站在车门旁，背面蓝墨水写着“第一批女司机”。纸张老化、冲印店标记、人物和街景都与年代吻合，旧展签草稿已经打印好，只差塞进展柜。
顾夏准备扫描时，看见背面角落一串被旧胶痕压住的铅笔号“TR-4/12”。捐赠登记只写“来自陈家旧物”，没有说明照片原来和什么放在一起。纸张、人物与街景仍然可信，她却把旧展签夹回文件夹，转去翻同批捐赠物的入藏清单。
清单把TR-4指向一组“1986春季驾驶培训宣传材料”。第12张正是这张照片；相邻照片里，同样六个人有人站在模拟方向盘旁，有人在课堂桌前。宣传册夹页上的课程表写着“候选学员12人，结业考核后分配岗位”。顾夏因此能确认六人处在培训活动中，却仍找不到六人都已正式上岗的记录。
第二天上午，她又在捐赠者父亲的工作手册里找到借片单：培训中心曾把TR-4这组照片借给车队宣传员制作招募海报，之后随宣传册归还。家庭后来整理遗物时，把照片单独塞进相册，宣传册另装一袋；入藏时两者又分到不同盒位。照片本身始终真实，变化发生在它与原来材料的关系被拆开以后。
距离闭馆布展只剩几个小时，顾夏没有撤掉照片，也没有把TR-4/12当成“六人都未上岗”的反证。她重写展签：“1986年女性公交驾驶培训班宣传照。现存材料可确认六人参加培训；其中几人后来正式上岗，仍需其他记录支持。”随后把扫描文件重新关联到宣传册页码、课程表、借片单和同批捐赠记录。
布展前一晚，照片终于装进展柜。背面的TR-4/12看不见了，新展签右下角却多了一行小字：“来源关系：TR-4/12，培训宣传材料组。”顾夏把那张写着“第一批女性公交司机合影”的旧展签草稿收进文件夹。
explanationParagraphs: The provenance principle holds that the meaning and evidential value of a record depend on its relationships of creation, use, custody, movement, and reorganization. Recovering those relationships helps determine what the record can actually support.

Provenance does not automatically prove content true and is not the same as authenticating an object. Its main role here is to explain and limit the evidential scope of the record. Gaps in custody or damage to original order should be recorded explicitly rather than repaired with a neat story.
explanationParagraphsZh: 来源原则强调记录的意义与证据价值依赖其创建、使用、保管、移动和重组关系。恢复这些关系能帮助判断记录到底支持什么。
来源关系不自动证明内容为真，也不等于鉴定真伪。它主要限制和解释记录的证据范围；保管空缺或原序受损应明确记录，不能用整齐故事补平。
articles.overall: The photograph remains an authentic 1986 photograph throughout; the problem is not a mistaken-material test or a discovery that it is fake. TR-4/12, the training publicity materials, course schedule, loan slip, and donation batch restore the record’s relationships of creation, use, and custody, separating “attended training” from “formally entered service.” Recovering provenance cannot prove who ultimately became a driver; it can only bring the label back within the range that the surviving records actually support.
articles.overallZh: 照片从始至终都是可信的1986年真实照片，问题不是标注笔误或真假鉴定。TR-4/12、培训宣传材料、课程表、借片单和捐赠批次恢复了它原先的创建、使用与保管关系，使“参加培训”与“正式上岗”重新分开。恢复来源关系不能证明谁最终上岗，只能让展签回到现有记录真正能支持的范围。

module.intro: An archival record can remain authentic yet acquire an overextended meaning after it is separated from the relationships of creation, use, and custody. Provenance preserves those relationships so description stays within what the surviving record can support.
module.diagramTitle: How provenance relationships constrain the evidential meaning of a genuine record
diagramSteps: Begin with the individual record and its existing description
Trace its identifier back to the original record group
Recover the chain of creation, use, and custody
Compare interpretations before and after the relationships were broken
Limit the claim to what the surviving relationships support and preserve the provenance information
diagramStepNotes: The paper, people, date, and street scene remain credible throughout, so the story does not depend on exposing a fake.
TR-4/12 reconnects the photograph to the Spring 1986 Driver Training Publicity Materials.
The course schedule and loan slip place the photograph within training and recruitment-publicity activities but do not record the six women’s final employment status.
The family album, separately bagged publicity booklet, and later placement in different archival boxes gradually break the original visible relationship and make a stronger interpretation easier.

The final label confirms only that all six attended training and explicitly states that later formal employment requires other records, showing provenance as a limit on interpretation rather than proof of content.
mapping: The genuine 1986 photograph → authentic content whose evidential meaning still depends on context.
TR-4/12 → the entry point for restoring the original record relationship.
The publicity booklet, course schedule, and loan slip → contexts of creation and use.
The photograph placed alone in an album and later in a separate box → custodial reorganization that breaks visible relationships.
The new label kept alongside the old draft → restoring provenance narrows the claim’s supported scope.
module.boundary: The provenance principle is not material authentication, dating, or the idea that finding an original box automatically proves a record’s content. Provenance relationships do not validate every statement in a record by themselves. They show who created the record, in what activity, how it was used, and how it was kept, helping define the range of evidence it can support. The museum, photograph, and people in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why does recovering TR-4/12 give Gu Xia stronger grounds to say that the six women attended training while still leaving her unable to say that all six later entered formal service?

moduleZh.intro: 档案记录离开创建、使用和保管关系后，仍可能真实，却被赋予过强的意义。来源原则保留这些关系，让说明停在现有记录真正能支持的位置。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 来源关系怎样限定一件真实记录的证据意义
diagramSteps: 先确认记录本身及其既有描述
追查编号与原始记录群的连接
恢复创建、使用与保管链条
比较关系断裂前后的解释差异
据现有关系限定主张并保留来源信息
diagramStepNotes: 照片的纸张、人物、年代和街景始终可信，因此不依赖赝品发现。
TR-4/12把照片重新接回1986春季驾驶培训宣传材料。
课程表和借片单说明照片处于培训与招募宣传活动中，但不记录六人最终岗位。
家庭相册、另装宣传册和入藏后的分盒使原有关系逐步断裂，造成更强解释。
最终展签只确认六人参加培训，并明确正式上岗仍需其他记录，体现来源关系限制而非证明内容。
mapping: 真实的1986照片 → 内容真实但证据意义仍需上下文。
TR-4/12 → 恢复原始记录关系的入口。
宣传册、课程表与借片单 → 创建和使用背景。
照片被单独收入相册并分盒 → 保管重组造成关系断裂。
新展签与旧草稿并存 → 恢复来源后主张范围被重新限定。
moduleZh.boundary: 来源原则不是材质鉴定、年代鉴定，也不是“找到原盒就能证明内容为真”。来源关系本身不会自动验证记录中的每个陈述；它说明记录由谁在何种活动中产生、怎样被使用和保管，从而帮助判断证据范围。本故事中的博物馆、照片与人物均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么恢复TR-4/12以后，顾夏能更有把握说“六人参加培训”，却仍不能据此说六人后来都正式上岗？

articles.fieldTitleZh: 图书馆、信息与档案研究
articles.title: The Loan Card in the Blue Violin Case
articles.titleZh: 蓝琴盒里的那张借用卡
articles.summary: On Saturday morning, Zhou Yu must assemble six violins by 9:30. V-12 is still in its blue case, but its loan card, three bows, and the afternoon performance point to different answers.
articles.summaryZh: 周六早上，周羽要在九点半前凑齐六套小提琴。蓝琴盒里的V-12还在，借用卡、三支弓和下午演出却指向不同答案。
storyParagraphs: At 8:40 on Saturday morning, two extra children arrived at the community music school, and Zhou Yu had to assemble six half-size violins by 9:30. Not a single violin was missing, and the regular teachers knew the old instruments well. But when she opened the blue case in B2, it contained only V-12 and its shoulder rest. The loan card still read: ‘Bow B-12 / Cabinet B2 / Permitted for off-site performance.’ The lesson began at 9:30, and the assistant had planned to start tuning and bow-hold practice at 9:15. Outside, the children were already lining up to have their arms measured.

Zhou Yu first looked for B-12. A note on the repair table said that B-12 had been sent for rehairing on Friday, and that V-12 had temporarily been paired with B-31 for an afternoon rehearsal and moved to B1. After rehearsal, a teacher had returned V-12’s blue case to its old empty space in B2, while B-31 stayed in B1 because it was for school use only. Both teachers on duty remembered those steps, but the loan card was still frozen at the state before Friday’s repair, and the shared record had only had its cabinet location changed once.

Zhou Yu opened the shared equipment record. V-12 was still listed in B1, its paired bow was still B-12, and its off-site permission still reflected V-12’s original status. V-12 was already booked for a small off-site performance that afternoon. If she trusted only the card in the blue case, she would go looking for B-12, which was still being repaired. If she relied only on memory from Friday’s rehearsal, she might pack B-31, which was not permitted off-site. On the spare rack she found B-18, currently unassigned to any other violin and permitted to leave the school. After checking its length and hair tension, she placed it beside V-12.

At 9:22, V-12 with B-18 stood beside five other violin sets outside the classroom. B-31 remained in B1, and B-12 was still under repair. The first group therefore began tuning seven minutes late, and the assistant had to skip one bow-hold exercise. While the children went into class, Zhou Yu changed the blue case card to B-18 and brought the shared record’s location, paired bow, and off-site relationship back into line with the physical set in front of her.

Before lunch, she and the repair teacher turned Friday’s changes into one continuous record: when B-12 had gone for rehairing, when V-12 had temporarily moved to B1 with B-31 for rehearsal, when it had returned to B2, and why it had been paired with B-18 for Saturday’s off-site performance. When another teacher came to collect the instrument for the afternoon performance, Zhou Yu was teaching in another room. He did not call her. Using V-12’s identity, B2 location, B-18 pairing, and off-site permission, he found the complete set on his own. After the performance, he recorded that V-12 had been returned to B2.

Before the cabinets were locked that evening, the blue case was settled back in B2. Its loan card still contained only a few lines: “V-12 / Bow B-18 / Cabinet B2 / Permitted for off-site performance.” In the final field, “Last updated,” there was now that day’s date and Zhou Yu’s initials.
storyParagraphsZh: 周六早上八点四十分，社区音乐学校临时多来两个孩子，周羽要在九点半前凑出六套二分之一小提琴。琴一把没丢，常驻老师也认得这些旧琴。可她打开B2里的蓝色琴盒时，里面只有V-12和肩托，借用卡还写着“配弓B-12／柜B2／可带出演出”。课程九点半开始，助教原定九点一刻带孩子调弦和练持弓，门外已经排着量手臂。
周羽先找B-12。维修桌上的纸条写着：周五B-12送去重装马尾，V-12下午排练时临时改配B-31，并搬到B1。排练结束后，有老师把V-12的蓝琴盒送回了原来的B2空位，B-31则留回B1，因为它只供校内练习。两位当班老师都记得这些动作，只是借用卡仍停在周五维修前，共享表只改过一次柜位。
周羽打开共享器材表：V-12的位置仍是B1，配弓却还是B-12，外借状态则沿用V-12原本可外出的条件。下午还有一场校外小演出预订V-12；如果只信蓝琴盒里的卡，她会去找正在维修的B-12，如果只信周五排练的记忆，又可能把不能外借的B-31装进去。她到备用架找到暂时未配给其他琴、可外借的B-18，试过长度和弓毛张力后放到V-12旁边。
九点二十二分，V-12配B-18和另外五套琴一起摆到教室门边，B-31仍留在B1，B-12还在维修。第一组孩子因此晚了七分钟开始调弦，助教少做了一轮持弓练习。周羽趁孩子进教室，把蓝琴盒借用卡改成B-18，也把共享表上的位置、配弓和外借关系对回眼前这套实物。
午休前，她和维修老师把周五的变化补成一条连续记录：B-12何时送修，V-12何时临时到B1配B-31排练，何时回到B2，以及周六为何改配B-18外出演出。下午负责演出的另一位老师来取琴时，周羽正在另一间教室。他没有打电话问她，只按V-12的身份、B2位置、B-18配弓和外借状态找到整套器材；演出归还后，又在记录里确认V-12仍回B2。
傍晚关柜前，蓝琴盒重新放稳在B2。盒内借用卡仍只有几行字：“V-12／配弓B-18／柜B2／可带出演出”。最下面“最后更新”一栏，多了当天日期和周羽的姓名缩写。
explanationParagraphs: Metadata uses stable identity, location, component relationships, events, permissions, and update responsibility so the same resource can be identified, found, assembled, used, and managed over time by different people.

Metadata is not the resource itself, and more is not always better. If only part of a record is updated, or maintenance stops, the record can gradually drift away from the physical object that still exists.
explanationParagraphsZh: 元数据用稳定身份、位置、部件关系、事件、权限和更新责任，使同一资源能被不同人识别、找到、组合、使用并持续管理。
元数据不是资源本身，也不是越多越好。记录若只更新一部分或停止维护，就会与仍然存在的实物逐渐分离。
articles.overall: The problem is not that one teacher forgot to change a card or that the equipment room is unmanaged. Friday’s repair simultaneously changed B-12’s status, V-12’s location, B-31’s temporary role, and the combination that could legally be taken off-site that afternoon, while the loan card, shared record, and personal memory each retained only part of those changes. What rules out the idea that “Zhou Yu just needs to remember” is the afternoon teacher’s ability, while Zhou Yu is elsewhere, to retrieve V-12 and B-18 independently from the aligned identity, location, pairing, event, and permission information, then complete the return update.
articles.overallZh: 问题不是某位老师忘记一张卡，也不是器材室无人管理。周五维修同时改变了B-12状态、V-12位置、B-31临时代用关系和下午外借可用组合，但借用卡、共享表和个人记忆各只保留了其中一部分。真正排除“靠周羽记住就行”的，是下午另一位老师在周羽不在场时，能依据已经对齐的身份、位置、配弓、事件和权限独立取走V-12并完成归还。

module.intro: Whether another teacher can collect the right instrument depends on its identity, location, bow pairing, repair history, and permission records still pointing to the physical set in front of them.
module.diagramTitle: How metadata keeps the same resource usable across people and tasks
diagramSteps: Use a stable identity to identify the specific resource
Record relationships among location, components, and permissions
Update maintenance, movement, and temporary substitution as events
Let different people complete different tasks from the same relationships
Record update responsibility so later changes remain traceable
diagramStepNotes: The V-12 identifier keeps the blue case, shared record, and physical violin tied to the same instrument.
B-12 under repair, B-31 for school use only, B-18 permitted off-site, and B1/B2 each represent different relationships that an old single card cannot replace.
V-12’s temporary move to B1 with B-31 for Friday rehearsal and later return to B2 show how one maintenance episode can alter several related facts at once.
The afternoon teacher finds V-12 with B-18 and checks the off-site permission without Zhou Yu present, showing that shared records—not personal memory—support use across shifts.
Confirming B2 on return and leaving an update date and initials gives the next person a way to judge whether the record still matches the physical equipment.
mapping: V-12 → stable resource identity.
B1/B2 and B-12, B-31, B-18 → location and component relationships.
Friday repair, temporary rehearsal pairing, and Saturday reassignment → the event chain that changes resource relationships.
“School use only” and “permitted for off-site performance” → usage permissions.
Update date and initials → maintenance responsibility and traceability.
module.boundary: Metadata is not the violin, bow, or repair itself, and clearer labels, more fields, or new software do not automatically solve the problem. Structured information is useful only when it is designed for specific identification, location, relationship, permission, and management tasks and kept in sync as objects change. Outdated, missing, or mutually inconsistent records can mislead just as easily. The school, people, and equipment in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: If all the teachers remembered what happened on Friday and none of the three bows was lost, why could the afternoon teacher reliably collect V-12 only after the identity, location, event, and permission information had been realigned?

moduleZh.intro: 同一把琴能不能被另一位老师准确取走，取决于编号、位置、配弓、维修与权限记录是否仍指向眼前实物。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 元数据怎样让同一资源跨人员、跨任务保持可用
diagramSteps: 用稳定身份识别具体资源
记录位置、部件和权限之间的关系
把维修、移动和临时代用作为事件更新
让不同人员据同一关系完成不同任务
记录更新责任，使资源变化继续可追查
diagramStepNotes: V-12编号使蓝琴盒、共享表和实物始终指向同一把琴。
B-12送修、B-31仅校内、B-18可外借以及B1/B2位置分别承担不同关系，不能由一张旧卡代替。
周五V-12临时到B1配B-31排练后又回B2，说明一次维护事件可以同时改变多项关联。
下午老师在周羽不在场时依记录找到V-12与B-18并核对外借状态，说明共同记录而非个人记忆支撑使用。
归还后确认B2并留下最后更新日期和姓名缩写，使下一班人员能判断记录是否仍贴近实物。
mapping: V-12 → 稳定的资源身份。
B1／B2与B-12、B-31、B-18 → 位置和部件关系。
周五送修、临时排练与周六改配 → 资源关系变化的事件链。
“仅校内练习”与“可带出演出” → 使用权限。
最后更新日期和姓名缩写 → 维护责任与可追查性。
moduleZh.boundary: 元数据不是小提琴、琴弓或维修本身，也不是贴清楚标签、增加字段或换软件就能自动解决。只有为具体识别、定位、关联、权限和管理任务设计，并在对象变化时共同维护的结构化信息才有作用；过时、遗漏或彼此不同步的记录同样会误导。本故事中的学校、人员和器材均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么周五所有老师都记得发生过什么、三支弓也都没有丢，下午那位老师仍只有在身份、位置、事件和权限被重新对齐后，才能在周羽不在场时可靠取走V-12？

references.use: Used to support how descriptive, administrative, and structural metadata help resources be discovered, understood, and managed, as well as the limits of standardization, quality, and ongoing maintenance.

references.use: Used to support recording preservation actions, conditions of use, and management responsibility through structured relationships among objects, events, rights, and agents.
